correctness.rationale: Using u_t=βu_(t-1)+(1-β)y_(t-1), bias-corrected v_t=u_t/(1-β^t), and ψ(v)=v/(1+v²), the exact scalar update is y_t=y_(t-1)-cψ(v_t). In the limiting autonomous map the ± symmetric orbit satisfies q=(1-β)/(1+β), 1+q²a²=cq/2, so a=√(s/2-1)/q exists uniquely iff s>2. At either phase the Jacobian has determinant β and trace 1+β-(1-β)cψ'(qa); the 3 Jury expressions equal 2(1+β)(4-s)/s, 4(1+β)(s-2)/s and 1-β, proving 2<s<4 exactly. The actual nonautonomous correction is O(β^t). For c=3, β≤.01, weighted sup norm max(|dy|,|du|/4), source first-step entry, derivative bound below 2/3 on paired radius .05 balls, and geometric forcing <=3β^t imply e_t<=.016(2/3)^(t-1). Independently checked symbolic Jury algebra and numerical recurrence over parameter endpoints including the claimed source interval; finite trajectories alone are not the proof. The objective limit is ρ(1-5β)(1+β)/(4h(1-β)²)>0.

It distinguishes the optimizer-specific Fisher/momentum nonlinearity from previously known Adam cycling.

final_claim: For scalar strongly convex quadratic f=h x²/2 under SOFIM first-moment Fisher regularization, the autonomous sign-symmetric nonzero two-cycle exists iff s=ηh(1-β)/[ρ(1+β)]>2 and is linearly asymptotically stable iff 2<s<4. For the actual bias-corrected source-initialized update with ηh/ρ=3 and 0≤β≤0.01, every initial normalized y0 within 0.01 of 1/√2 converges geometrically to the alternating nonminimizing orbit.
